clue.text: The cabin-boy, perhaps, little beast!

definitions.meaning: a ship's boy is a young scamp who lives at sea, a seagoing urchin
a small spiny creature of the seabed

explanation.surface: Someone exasperated by a mischievous youngster aboard ship calls him a little beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiny echinoderm of the shore is literally an urchin of the sea, and a ship's lad is a scamp afloat.

clue.text: Firm animals kept in one

definitions.meaning: horses are housed in this farm building

explanation.surface: Someone notes that the animals in a building are kept firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady describes something firm, and a building housing horses is a stall block of that name.

clue.text: All decked out for war machines

definitions.text: All decked out for war machines

parts.words: All decked out for war machines
parts.note: decked suggests dressed up, but here it means given a flight deck on which warplanes are parked

explanation.surface: Everything is dressed up smartly for the weapons of war.
explanation.definitionFit: A warship with a long flat flight deck carries military planes, so it is fitted out with a deck for war machines.

clue.text: Gets new men in, shaking cruet, sir!

indicators.note: a cruet is shaken over food, and the shaking here jumbles the letters

explanation.surface: Someone tells a man that he is bringing in new staff while shaking the condiment set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaking' mixes the letters of CRUET and SIR together.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlisting new staff or soldiers is to sign up fresh members.

clue.text: It's held to be the way to deal with something

definitions.text: It's held to be the way to deal with something

parts.words: It's held to be the way to deal with something
parts.note: the grip you hold on a door or tool, and also a verb meaning to manage a matter

explanation.surface: A general statement that something is thought to be the right approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held to be' reads as 'believed to be', but it also points to the part of an object that is gripped.
explanation.definitionFit: A grip on a pan is held by the hand, and to manage a problem is to cope with it.

clue.text: Tell-tale ran up with the king to a hill

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word ran is read from bottom to top

parts.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A sneak runs uphill with the monarch to a summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses RAN to NAR. 'Tell-tale' looks like a sneak, but read literally it is one who tells a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A storyteller is literally a teller of a tale.

clue.text: We hear, chuck position in the Orient

indicators.note: we hear tells you the word for chuck is only heard, and the spelling differs

parts.note: to chuck is to throw, or cast

explanation.surface: Gossip says someone has been thrown out of their post in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' signals that CAST, a throw, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindu society in India was divided into hereditary classes, so one's rank there is a social class of that kind.

clue.text: Follows, with a catch in mind!

definitions.text: Follows, with a catch in mind!

parts.words: Follows, with a catch in mind!
parts.note: someone pursuing with intent to catch, as a hunter or police officer does

explanation.surface: Someone who follows another while hiding an ulterior motive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a catch' sounds like a hidden snag, but it means capturing the quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: Pursuing someone to capture them is running after them.

clue.text: Find places for lots of senior citizens? How vengeful to do it

definitions.text: Find places for lots of senior citizens?
definitions.meaning: to settle is to house, and scores of old folk are many elderly people
the vengeful pay back old grudges

explanation.surface: A housing officer's task of homing many pensioners, oddly linked to revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty, so 'lots of senior citizens' read whimsically gives the answer's words in the first reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking revenge for a past wrong is paying back a grudge, idiomatically.

clue.text: Last to finish chopped, bitter herb

parts.note: the end is the finish

indicators.note: herbs are chopped in cooking, and here the herb's letters are cut up and rearranged

parts.note: rue is a bitter-tasting herb

explanation.surface: A cook's instruction to finish off with some chopped bitter herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped' rearranges RUE into URE. 'Last' looks like a word meaning final, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to go on enduring, survive over time.

clue.text: A native of this continent takes a point

indicators.note: the continent takes on the extra letter at its end

parts.note: the continent of the native in question, Africa
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone from a continent makes a point.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Africa is a person born on that continent.

clue.text: Destroyed a dye taken away stirred, then cooked

indicators.note: stirred describes the letters being mixed, as a cook stirs a pot

explanation.surface: A ruined batch of dye is removed and stirred, then heated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken away' removes D, Y, E from DESTROYED A, leaving E S T R O D A, which 'stirred' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat that has been baked in the oven has been cooked by dry heat.

clue.text: Go, taken by soldiers, for instance

definitions.meaning: soldiers take time off duty as a furlough

explanation.surface: An order to go, given by troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart is to go away, and time off granted to troops is a furlough.

clue.text: Old flame has a danger to shipping to check

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
a sea mine is an explosive hazard for ships

explanation.surface: A former lover has a hazard at sea to inspect.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect something closely is to check it.

clue.text: Stood by some cities in war!

definitions.text: Stood by some cities in war!

parts.words: Stood by some cities in war!
parts.note: stood by sounds like supported, but means endured, as encircled and blockaded cities like Leningrad did

explanation.surface: Some cities stood firm and loyal during wartime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stood by' suggests loyalty; read as 'endured', it is what a besieged city does.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockade surrounding a town in war is something the townsfolk must endure.

clue.text: For jobs, enquire within, a little way back

indicators.note: within says one word sits inside the other
back means the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: St is the short form of street, a little way
to enquire is to ask

explanation.surface: Job adverts telling applicants to enquire inside, a short distance back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little way' is street, abbreviated as usual on maps; 'back' and 'within' are both indicators acting on it and on the word for enquire.
explanation.definitionFit: Duties or chores to do are pieces of work.

clue.text: Fight a hard one

definitions.meaning: a hard one suggests a tough task, a great effort

explanation.surface: Describing a tough battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussle is a fight, and a difficult effort is a hard slog.

clue.text: Not one with authority, as it were!

definitions.text: Not one with authority, as it were!

parts.words: Not one with authority, as it were!
parts.note: not one in power, but also one who is not with, that is against, those in authority

explanation.surface: Someone who holds no official power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' reads as 'having', but it also means 'on the side of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutineer is one who opposes those in charge.

clue.text: Symptom of vulgarity suggests a nasty smack, it seems!

definitions.meaning: a lack of refinement or style
smack means a flavour, so a nasty one is an unpleasant flavour

explanation.surface: A rude slap reveals coarseness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smack' looks like a slap, but it also means a flavour, as in 'smacks of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse style shows poor judgement, and an unpleasant flavour is literally a foul savour.

clue.text: To impress? Certainly to make one's mark

definitions.meaning: to imprint, press a mark into something
to leave an imprint, as with a rubber die

explanation.surface: A question about making an impact, answered with a yes.
explanation.definitionFit: To imprint is to press a design on, and an inked die leaves a mark.

clue.text: Hops in and out of a apres, surmised bottle

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Hops in and out of a apres, surmised bottle' is garbled OCR: HOPS IN is an anagram of the answer but the anagram indicator and link text are corrupted, and no scan or search gives the printed clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Hops in and out of a apres, surmised bottle

clue.text: Aspire to change some favourable words

indicators.note: to change says the letters of aspire are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone ambitious hopes to alter some kind remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Compliments and commendation are kind words.

clue.text: Hurt, they're getting a kick from it

definitions.text: Hurt, they're getting a kick from it

parts.words: Hurt, they're getting a kick from it
parts.note: kick suggests being struck, but here means a thrill: cruel people enjoy pain inflicted

explanation.surface: People injured by being kicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting a kick' reads as being struck, but means enjoying.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who take pleasure in cruelty enjoy inflicting pain.

clue.text: Piece of ridicule to despatch higher?

definitions.meaning: to send something upward, read literally

explanation.surface: A mocking piece is sent upstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A parody mocks its target, and posting something aloft is literally sending it skyward.

clue.text: They join things with threads

parts.note: threads suggests sewing, but these are the spiral ridges of a metal fastener

explanation.surface: Tailors stitch things together with cotton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'threads' suggests needle and cotton, but it means the spiral grooves of a metal fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiral metal fasteners hold pieces together by their helical ridges.

clue.text: Wake up sure, confused about nothing

indicators.note: about means the anagram goes around the zero
confused means the letters of sure are mixed up

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone woken up is certain yet muddled about nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges SURE to RUSE, and 'about' puts it around O.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir someone from sleep is to waken them.

clue.text: Coming down hard on the sort of welcome Caesar often got!

definitions.meaning: frozen pellets falling from the sky

definitions.text: the sort of welcome Caesar often got
definitions.meaning: Romans greeted their leader with 'Hail, Caesar!'

explanation.surface: Caesar is welcomed harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice pellets falling are a storm of that kind, and greeting with 'Ave' was saluting.

clue.text: Have a right to Eve's Red revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive gives the letters E V E S

explanation.surface: Eve's communist rebel is owed something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' anagrams EVES RED. 'Red' looks like a communist, but it is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit something is to be entitled to it.

clue.text: Loner, venal? Some cheek!

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is outraged at being called a corrupt loner.
explanation.definitionFit: Audacity or impudence is cheek.

clue.text: Important ladies back me for publishing newspapers, etc

indicators.note: for links the pronoun to the following piece in a charade
back means the word me is turned round

parts.note: presses are printing machines, and the press is newspapers etc

explanation.surface: Grand ladies support me on behalf of the newspaper industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like support, but it reverses ME into EM.
explanation.definitionFit: Female rulers of empires are royal women of the highest rank.
